events.title: Belisarius enters Rome unopposed as the Gothic garrison withdraws
events.description: The citizens of Rome, mindful of the fate of Naples, put up no resistance to Justinian's general Belisarius, and the 4,000-strong Gothic garrison withdrew. Belisarius went on to take Ravenna in 540.

events.title: The Khazars destroy an Umayyad army at Marj Ardabil
events.description: Near Ardabil in north-western Iran, a Khazar army led by Barjik destroyed the forces of the Umayyad Caliphate and killed their commander, al-Jarrah ibn Abdallah al-Hakami. The Khazars then raided deep into the caliphate as far as northern Mesopotamia.

events.title: Malcolm IV, the 'Maiden King' of Scotland, dies
events.description: Malcolm IV died unmarried at 24, after a reign in which he surrendered Northumbria and Cumbria to Henry II of England. His brother William the Lion succeeded him and reigned for 49 years.

events.title: Juan Diego reports a vision of the Virgin at Tepeyac
events.description: According to tradition, the Virgin Mary appeared to the Indigenous convert Juan Diego on the hill of Tepeyac near Mexico City. The image of Our Lady of Guadalupe became Mexico's most revered religious symbol.
events.html: According to tradition, the Virgin Mary appeared to the Indigenous convert Juan Diego on the hill of Tepeyac near Mexico City. The image of Our Lady of Guadalupe became Mexico's most revered religious symbol.

events.title: Williamite dragoons rout an Irish Army detachment at Reading
events.description: Dutch States Army dragoons under Hans Bentinck, supported by Williamite civilians, routed an Irish Army detachment under Patrick Sarsfield from Reading in Berkshire. It was one of only two substantial battles fought in England during the Glorious Revolution.

events.title: Jerusalem surrenders to British forces
events.description: The mayor of Jerusalem surrendered the city to the British army, ending four centuries of Ottoman rule. General Allenby entered on foot two days later.
events.html: The mayor of Jerusalem surrendered the city to the British army, ending four centuries of Ottoman rule. General Allenby entered on foot two days later.

events.title: British forces launch Operation Compass in Egypt
events.description: British and Commonwealth troops attacked Italian camps in western Egypt. In two months they advanced 500 miles and took some 130,000 prisoners, before Rommel's arrival turned the tide.

events.title: Tanganyika becomes independent
events.description: Tanganyika became independent from Britain, with Julius Nyerere as prime minister. In 1964 it united with Zanzibar to form Tanzania.
